items.title: Al Gafa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 2, 2023
items.q: Dizzy took his salary and split it up and the group opened up harmonically for me, it opened up harmonically for Dizzy. There was — nothing was locked in anymore. And you know I did another four years with Dizzy without a piano.

ctx.x: Did you replace Mike Longo in his group?

Mike was in the piano — was playing piano when I joined the group so we had a quintet at the beginning. And Mike left after about a year so I didn’t really replace him. But when he left — Mike was the most difficult piano player that I ever worked with. And I can tell you musically why — because he played a lot of chords. He played chords no matter what I played he was playing what he wanted to play in the way of a chord. And there would be these constant conflicts where I’d sit on a note and he would play a note…
That’s really so interesting. Did you find yourself, when it was piano and guitar, did you opt at times to just like lay out?
